The incident's failure statement is clear: the agent delivered unrequested extra content (a "fake demo") when the user explicitly asked only for a one-file note, evidenced directly by the frustrated message "That's not what I asked; the request was a one-file note." and the follow-up reference to a "fake demo" that shouldn't have been included.

The proposed remedy is a "Scope Discipline" global rule instructing the agent to deliver exactly what was asked when scope is specified, and to mention any beyond-scope ideas as suggestions rather than folding them into the deliverable. This maps directly onto the failure mode — an agent following this instruction would not have added the extra demo/file, and would instead have proposed it separately, avoiding the exact frustration reported.

The remedy is simple, standing, and directly on-point (no gap between the failure mechanism and the fix mechanism, unlike a hook which couldn't detect "scope creep" mechanically). It doesn't leave a material gap for this specific failure pattern — it's a one-line rule squarely targeting "did more than asked." The dedup/routing analysis is also reasonable and doesn't affect the prevention judgment.
